rationale: Implement four persistent domain services and three deterministic contract-backed mocks under local Docker Compose. Retain protected-operation authorization despite simulated identity; derive principals from trusted identity validation, not command fields. Keep production user lifecycle, real settlement/delivery, percentage attendance, gateway, Kubernetes and vector infrastructure outside scope. Git-versioned rationale JSON provides decision memory without premature infrastructure. Revision 1.1.0 records a known limitation: the paid-cancellation refund workflow is designed and contracted but not implemented in Registration, which rejects cancellation of a confirmed paid registration with 409 REFUND_WORKFLOW_REQUIRED and keeps the seat (fail closed).
invariants: Participants access only their own resources; organizers are restricted to their organization.
Global administrators manage events/activities and read reports across organizations but do not administer users or organizations.
Invalid identity or unavailable Identity fails closed; protected requests never downgrade to anonymous access.
Internal service operations and mock controls are not public authorization bypasses.
Certificate issuance requires confirmed registration, an idempotent check-in and completed activity.
Business and operational configuration is external and validated without silent permissive defaults.
Real credentials and .env files are never committed or logged.
Mocks and documentation checks cannot substitute for real database/broker integration evidence or the required 95 percent domain mutation gate.
A confirmed paid seat is never released without an approved refund; until the refund workflow exists, its cancellation is rejected with REFUND_WORKFLOW_REQUIRED.
